appraisal_events.evidence: « On n'est pas obligé d'inviter tout le monde ; est-ce qu'il m'invite ? Je ne connais pas sa femme. » ; « la famille de Swann leur semblait du même genre que beaucoup d'autres familles d'agents de change » ; « des financiers d'un cran supérieur à son grand-père »
appraisal_events.explanation: The parents deny Swann any special standing: the mother justifies dropping him from her invitations and disclaims his wife, and both parents rank his house, family and stockbroker grandfather as ordinary specimens surpassed elsewhere. The narrator's closing frame (they are « dépourvus de ce sens supplémentaire ») quietly undercuts their verdict rather than endorsing it.

appraisal_events.evidence: « m'émerveillant du prodige que j'existasse dans l'esprit de Swann » ; « Mon imagination avait isolé et consacré dans le Paris social une certaine famille »
appraisal_events.explanation: Against his parents' flatness, the narrator treats Swann's mere recollection of him as a prodigy and has privately consecrated the Swann family as unique. The mature narrator marks this consecration as his alone (« ces ornements, j'étais seul à les voir »), so the admiration is reported with irony rather than endorsed.

status_effects.explanation: Locally Swann loses standing in the family's reckoning: he is no longer invited, his wife is not acknowledged, and his house and lineage are graded as unremarkable next to better-placed houses and higher-ranked financiers.
The boy gains emotionally from learning that he exists as a defined person in Swann's mind — name, mother, family, address — a discovery he receives as a marvel.

ambiguities: The passage is double-edged about whose appraisal it backs: the parents are said to lack an organ of perception (the infra-red analogy implies a real « quantité inconnue » around Gilberte), yet the narrator concedes the ornaments were his alone and that his extra sense was « momentané » and lent by love — so the deflation of Swann is neither plainly endorsed nor plainly ridiculed.

Odette is present only as « sa femme » and is never named; she is the stated ground of the mother's refusal to invite Swann, so the snub may be read as attaching to the marriage rather than to Swann himself.
